digest.component_or_area: store lock management (mkdir and fcntl dual-leg locking)
propositions: On platforms without /proc (macOS), _process_start_time always returns None, making the recycled-pid branch unsatisfiable and causing dead processes with recycled pids to be misjudged as live indefinitely
When current_start is None (unqualified liveness verdict), the lock should be reclaimed if its age exceeds the 1h ceiling, not exempted as it is now
A genuinely live owner with matching stamped and current start times must never be reclaimed on a timer, even past the ceiling
The owner-less-dir reclamation path must be bounded by the ceiling when the rmdir fails, currently leaving an owner-less dir until the ceiling kicks in via the owner-unreadable branch
The fix requires splitting lock.py (798 LOC) into lock.py (~510 LOC) and lock_owner.py (~339 LOC) to stay within the 800 LOC module size limit

All references to moved lock functions in test files (12 patch-string and 42 attribute-access sites) must be repointed to lock_owner without re-export shims to preserve the behavior-preserving migration
